Throughput is in BYTES per second, which is what Chrome's
_page_weight_note: R40: 'initial HTML + CSS + district JSON under 60 KB gzipped'. 60 KB = 61440 bytes.
Counted as what the browser must have before the page is readable and the dropdowns
work: the document, every stylesheet it links, and every script it loads. Anything
fetched after first paint is not in this number and is bounded separately below.
_script_note: A tighter ceiling on JavaScript alone: 12 KB gzipped for site.js + address.js
together, measured at 6.7 KB. The 60 KB page budget is loose enough that a
framework could hide inside it, and §2 decides vanilla ES modules with no bundler
and no runtime dependency — a claim about the code that only stays true if it is a
number somewhere. React with its DOM package is about 45 KB gzipped, so anything
of that shape trips this long before it troubles the page budget.
_geometry_note: §6A.3: simplified district geometry, fetched after first paint, budget 300 KB
gzipped. Measured at 132 KB at the pinned 2.2 m tolerance. It is only fetched when
a street address is submitted, so it is never on the critical path of a district
number, a ZIP, a neighbourhood, a dropdown choice or a shared /district/N link.
_runs_note: §6A asks for p95 over at least 20 runs. With 20 samples the p95 is the 19th
ordered value, so a single slow run does not pass and a single fast one does not

3g-fast.label: 3G Fast, as WebPageTest defines it, plus a mid-tier Android CPU

3g-slow.label: Chrome DevTools' own Slow 3G preset — reported, never gated

_profile_note: Two profiles, one gate. '3g-fast' is the promise: it is the profile R40's 3 s was
written against and the one CI fails on.
'3g-slow' is measured and printed and never gated, because a 2000 ms round trip
spends 6 s on three sequential round trips before a single byte of ours is
considered. Under that profile the number says nothing about our page weight — it
measures the network. Gating on it would mean the only way to pass is to stop
loading a stylesheet. It is reported so the figure is on the record rather than
Both figures are CI measurements on a reference profile, never observed field
percentiles. There is no real-user monitoring because analytics are banned, and
§2 says so out loud: SLA evidence is synthetic, and we say so.
